correctness.rationale: For intersecting cosets, the negative Fourier coefficients occur exactly in J-perp outside the two larger annihilators, yielding 1+2(1-alpha)(1-beta). For disjoint cosets, character orthogonality and the order of displacement in G/(H+K) give the exact polygon average. A cut-plane contour formula gives alternating strictly positive Fourier coefficients as moments of a positive measure; root-of-unity filtering proves the full even/odd hierarchy. Endpoint Laplace asymptotics and the r=1 rational Fourier coefficients give the two distinct sharp convergence laws. Boundary cases H=K, nested subgroups, coincident cosets and m=2 are included. A fresh checker passed 5,594 separate direct-transform/polygon numerical assertions; these supplement rather than establish the infinite-index claims.

value.rationale: Two cosets are the minimal interacting building blocks of the coset-ring norm problem. The exact formula resolves all relative intersection and displacement regimes, and the order envelope identifies the globally strongest and weakest cancellation orders with sharp realizability. The unexpected exponential-to-algebraic transition at equal subgroup ratios is quantitative information not supplied by subadditivity, the standard single-coset formula, or generic coset decomposition bounds. This finite-dimensional invariant is natural and fully classified rather than an arbitrary slice.
